RESULT [continual]: COCO 40+40: 53.0 AP vs 54.5 for joint training. COCO 70+10: 52.4 vs 57.2. Updating only 12% of kernels worked best. Existing benchmarks reuse each image in 1.84 stages on average, and removing that leakage costs methods 0.6-2.0 AP.
US [continual]: Fisher-based selective kernel updating is the detector version of the professor's 'freeze most, train a little' idea, and it is a principled alternative to arbitrary backbone freezing. Fisher-based differential kernel importance, 12% of kernels in incremental stages (20% in the base stage). The 1.84 average stage reuse is for the 20+20 four-stage setting.
